alternate_names: Sri Ganesh Temple, Secunderabad Railway Station
deities: Lord Ganesha (idol with unique posture: right hand on thigh, another hand holding the Ankusham, left hand on the trunk, fourth hand holding a Damarakam with a snake/Nagumpamu)
festivals: Sankashti Chaturthi (also called Sankat Haran Chaturthi)

history.period: Idol discovered 1824; temple built thereafter per Agama Shastras; extended in 1960
history.summary: Sri Ganesh Temple near the Secunderabad Railway Station (Regimental Bazar Main Road) is one of the oldest and most important Ganesh temples of the twin cities, about 200 years old (identity confirmed; no other serious candidate for a 'Sri Ganesh Temple' in Secunderabad). Legend: in 1824 soldiers of the Madras Regiment discovered the Vinayaka idol while digging a well; it was installed per the Agama Shastras - the idol is considered unique for its posture (right hand on thigh, ankusham, left hand on trunk, damarakam with a snake). One source says the idol was installed by the Kanchi Peetham Shankaracharya (verify). Sub-shrine idols of Subrahmanya and Anjaneya were consecrated in 1932. The temple underwent an extension in 1960; annual revenue reported around Rs. 4 crore (per temple committee chairman, in one source - verify). Daily Ganapati Homam and Nitya Kalyanam are held; it draws heavy crowds at Vinayaka Chavithi and Sankashti Chaturthi.

name: Sri Ganesh Temple, Secunderabad
town_description: Secunderabad is the twin city of Hyderabad, originally a British cantonment, falling in Hyderabad district of Telangana. The temple stands on Ganesh Temple Station Road / Regimental Bazar Main Road, next to the Secunderabad Railway Station in the Shivaji Nagar / Regimental Bazaar area.

travel.airport: Rajiv Gandhi International Airport, Hyderabad - about 30-35 km (verify).
travel.railway: Secunderabad Junction - within walking distance of the temple (verify).
travel.road: Regimental Bazar Main Road, next to Secunderabad railway station and bus stand; city buses and autos; paid parking nearby, tight during festivals (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: Vinayaka Chavithi (August-September) is the most festive; early morning 6:00-7:00 AM for peaceful darshan.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Sources conflict: 6:00 AM - 12:30 PM and 4:00 - 9:00 PM (templesnow); 5:30 AM - 1:00 PM and 4:00 - 8:30 PM (renukaastrology). Verify before visiting. Entry free; Ganapati Homam around 8:20 AM, Nitya Kalyanam around 11:00 AM (per holidify; verify).
